rows.justification: Lead volume and monthly/weekly lead-side evolution are observed for the canonical period.

depth.comparison: Monthly distribution from April partial through July partial.
depth.interpretation: Volume is substantial and concentrated in June, with July partial still active.
depth.business_implication: Scale is available for optimization decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: April and July are partial months.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Volume is sufficient for aggregate product analysis.

rows.justification: FARO tier distribution and A/B denominator are available.

depth.evidence: 67 Tier A, 402 Tier B, 469 A/B, 648 Tier C, 432 Tier D.
depth.comparison: A/B and Tier A shares versus total leads.
depth.interpretation: Quality exists but high-quality Tier A is a small share.
depth.business_implication: Optimization should improve lead mix, not only volume.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: FARO is quality proxy; revenue unavailable.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: A/B share is 30.28%; Tier A share is 4.33%.

rows.justification: Canonical matched commercial metrics are calculable and coverage states are explicit.

depth.evidence: Matched universe: 1362 leads, 396 A/B, 55 Tier A, 1069.05 EUR spend.
depth.comparison: Matched versus lead_only and spend_only.
depth.interpretation: Matched cost-quality is efficient on observed metrics; unmatched coverage remains separate.
depth.business_implication: Use matched metrics for economic decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Temporal spend evidence is partial; rejected queries are excluded.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: cost_per_ab_commercial_matched is 2.70 EUR.

rows.justification: Campaign/adset lead quality is available, but spend lacks native campaign/adset fields and is derived from ad-level reconciliation.
rows.impact: Campaign/adset economic ranking should be treated as diagnostic, not definitive.

depth.evidence: Campaign/adset lead quality exists; top adset has 1267 leads and 370 A/B. Derived commercial spend is available only through ad-level reconciliation.
depth.comparison: Campaign/adset lead quality versus ad-level matched commercial spend derivation.
depth.interpretation: Structure-level quality can be diagnosed, while direct campaign/adset economics remain partial.
depth.business_implication: Use campaign/adset reads as diagnostics and keep economic decisions at matched ad-level evidence.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: fct_spend does not expose direct campaign/adset identifiers in the acquired evidence.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Campaign/adset analysis is partially covered and should not be used as definitive economic ranking.

rows.justification: Ad-level evidence includes ad_id_norm, ad_name and metrics, but some rows are lead_only/spend_only and creative causality is prohibited.
rows.impact: Ad views support concentration and diagnostics, not causal creative winner claims.

depth.evidence: Ad-level evidence includes ad_id_norm, ad_name, lead_count, A/B, Tier A and matched commercial spend where available.
depth.comparison: Matched, lead_only and spend_only ad coverage states are separated.
depth.interpretation: Ad diagnostics are reliable for concentration and reconciliation status, but not for creative causality.
depth.business_implication: Use ad-level data to manage coverage and concentration; avoid creative winner claims.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: ad_name is descriptive only and creative metadata beyond ad_name is unavailable.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Ad-level analysis is partially covered for diagnostics and excluded for causal creative interpretation.

rows.justification: FARO/ticket intent and product/form signals are available and strongly separate observed quality.

depth.evidence: tiene_billetes true has 195 A/B of 218 leads; false has 274 A/B of 1331.
depth.comparison: Intent status true versus false and ticket_status categories.
depth.interpretation: Intent/status is the strongest observed separator.
depth.business_implication: Pre-qualification and optimization signals matter more than raw volume.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Association only; not revenue or causality.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Intent variables explain quality differences better than aggregate volume.

rows.justification: The evidence supports a clear volume-quality-cost trade-off in the matched universe and coverage states.

depth.evidence: High volume and low matched costs coexist with limited Tier A share.
depth.comparison: Volume versus A/B/Tier A quality and matched economics.
depth.interpretation: The optimization problem is lead mix, not just lead price.
depth.business_implication: Meta decisions should balance scale against intent-qualified quality.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Coverage prevents full economic comparison for lead_only groups.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Main trade-off is scale efficiency versus qualified intent mix.

rows.justification: Concentration by campaign/adset and top ads is observable.

depth.evidence: The main captacion adset has 1267 of 1549 leads; the top ad has 643 leads.
depth.comparison: Top structures versus remaining structures.
depth.interpretation: A few units dominate scale and learning.
depth.business_implication: Dependency risk should be managed before aggressive scaling.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Concentration is not proof of creative superiority.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: There is material concentration risk.

rows.justification: Monthly and weekly lead quality exist, but weekly comparability and temporal spend-quality are partial.
rows.impact: Temporal conclusions are limited to lead-side quality stability, not cost-quality trend.

depth.evidence: Monthly lead quality is available for April partial through July partial; weekly lead quality is available.
depth.comparison: Monthly/weekly lead-side quality exists, while temporal commercial spend queries were rejected.
depth.interpretation: Lead-side temporal stability can be described, but temporal cost-quality cannot.
depth.business_implication: Use the temporal view for quality monitoring, not weekly or monthly budget efficiency decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: April and July are partial months; first and last weeks are partial; spend temporal evidence is rejected.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Temporal analysis is partially covered by lead-side quality only.

rows.justification: Recommendations are derived from stabilized Knowledge and classified by SPEC-014.

depth.evidence: Knowledge Set identifies intent quality, coverage gaps, concentration and temporal limits.
depth.comparison: Actions are separated into experiments, verifiable action and non-actionable hypothesis.
depth.interpretation: Only testable or auditable actions are proposed.
depth.business_implication: Optimization can proceed without converting observations into unsupported decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Budget reallocation and creative winner claims remain excluded.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: There are three actionable recommendations and one non-actionable hypothesis.

rows.justification: Coverage states, limitations, rejected queries and UNKNOWNs are explicit.

depth.evidence: matched, lead_only, spend_only and rejected MCP queries are documented.
depth.comparison: Usable evidence versus rejected and unavailable evidence.
depth.interpretation: The product preserves material limits close to affected decisions.
depth.business_implication: Decision-makers can distinguish reliable metrics from partial reads.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Some temporal and revenue questions remain unresolved.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Limitations are sufficient for transparent product acceptance.

rows.justification: Platform is available in the authorized lead source, but platform-level spend economics are not available in the acquired evidence.
rows.impact: Platform comparison is limited to lead quality and cannot support platform budget reallocation.

depth.evidence: fb has 1047 leads, 329 A/B and 44 Tier A; ig has 502 leads, 140 A/B and 23 Tier A.
depth.comparison: fb A/B rate is 31.42%; ig A/B rate is 27.89%.
depth.interpretation: Observed lead quality differs modestly by platform, but cost-quality by platform is unavailable.
depth.business_implication: Platform signals can guide diagnostics, not spend decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: No approved platform spend allocation was acquired.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Platform quality is observable with partial economic coverage.

rows.justification: Ticket status is available in the authorized lead source, but it is not a revenue or sales conversion validation.
rows.impact: Ticket status may be used as an intent-quality diagnostic, not as proof of sale conversion.

depth.evidence: solo_mirando has 955 leads and 53 A/B; en_proceso has 376 leads and 221 A/B; tiene_billetes has 218 leads and 195 A/B.
depth.comparison: A/B rate increases from 5.55% in solo_mirando to 89.45% in tiene_billetes.
depth.interpretation: Ticket status strongly separates observed FARO quality.
depth.business_implication: Intent qualification is a reliable diagnostic input for lead quality decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: The field does not prove revenue, booking, or sales completion.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Ticket status is usable as quality evidence with revenue limits.

rows.justification: No separate current CAPI/event evidence beyond authorized lead fields was acquired for this product.
rows.impact: CAPI or event maturity cannot be evaluated in this execution.

depth.evidence: The consulted sources are fct_lead_enriched, fct_spend, dim_campaign_signal and int_faro_lead_scoring.
depth.comparison: No acquired artifact contains event-level CAPI delivery, match quality or browser/server event diagnostics.
depth.interpretation: The question is outside available evidence for this package.
depth.business_implication: No tracking-maturity recommendation is made.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: CAPI status remains not_available.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: CAPI/event evaluation requires a separate authorized evidence source.

rows.justification: Tier A volume is available, but its low share makes fine-grained Tier A conclusions sensitive to denominators.
rows.impact: Tier A can support aggregate diagnostics, while small-segment Tier A reads require caution.

depth.evidence: There are 67 Tier A leads globally and 55 Tier A leads in the matched commercial universe.
depth.comparison: Tier A is 4.33% of total leads; A/B is 30.28%.
depth.interpretation: Tier A exists but is sparse relative to total volume.
depth.business_implication: Use A/B for broader optimization and Tier A as a stricter guardrail.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Small Tier A counts reduce stability in narrow breakdowns.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Tier A evidence is valid but partial for detailed segmentation.

rows.justification: Creative metadata beyond ad_name was not available in the acquired evidence.
rows.impact: Creative analysis is restricted to ad-level diagnostics and cannot infer creative drivers.

depth.evidence: Ad evidence contains ad_id_norm and ad_name with lead and spend metrics.
depth.comparison: No visual asset, hook taxonomy, format metadata or creative attribute table was acquired.
depth.interpretation: ad_name is descriptive and not a causal creative dimension.
depth.business_implication: Creative winner claims remain excluded.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Creative metadata remains not_available.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: A creative analysis requires separate authorized creative metadata.

rows.justification: No revenue or sales conversion source was included in the authorized acquisition.
rows.impact: The product cannot evaluate revenue efficiency or return on ad spend.

depth.evidence: The Evidence Set declares revenue or sales conversion efficiency as not_available.
depth.comparison: Available quality metrics are FARO tiers and intent fields, not sales outcomes.
depth.interpretation: Economic conclusions stop at spend per lead and spend per FARO-qualified lead.
depth.business_implication: Revenue decisions require additional authorized sales data.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: Revenue/sales conversion remains not_available.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: No revenue optimization claim is supported.

rows.justification: Weekly lead quality is available, but complete weekly cost-quality is unavailable because temporal spend queries were rejected by provider cost policy.
rows.impact: Weekly interpretation is limited to lead-side quality, not spend efficiency trend.

depth.evidence: Weekly lead quality was acquired; weekly commercial spend was rejected by ERR_COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
depth.comparison: Monthly and weekly lead-side quality exist; temporal spend-quality does not.
depth.interpretation: Temporal quality can be monitored, but economic trend is incomplete.
depth.business_implication: Do not use this package for weekly budget pacing decisions.
depth.limitation_or_uncertainty: First and last weeks are partial and cost-quality is unavailable.
depth.conclusion_or_hypothesis: Weekly question is partially covered by quality evidence only.
